children: Palm oil rises in Asian trading, supported by soybean oil's gains overnight on the Chicago Board of Trade. Technical analysis suggests crude palm oil futures are showing signs of recovery, improving short-term sentiment, AmInvestment Bank says in a note. If prices remain above 4,279 ringgit a ton, upward momentum could persist, with any intraday pullback likely to attract renewed buying interest, it adds. AmInvestment Bank expects crude palm oil futures to find resistance at 4,361 ringgit a ton and support at 4,251 ringgit a ton. The Bursa Malaysia Derivatives contract for February delivery is 47 ringgit higher at 4,339 ringgit a ton. (yingxian.wong@wsj.com)
